audited_source_corrections.action: Insert the missing comma in the G1c conjunction-contraction conclusion, put the left biconditional's conclusion on the left of the turnstile, and call the displayed final object a sequent rather than a formula.
audited_source_corrections.source_issue_or_choice: The frozen G1c simulation displays A-and-B Gamma with no comma, breaking the sequent context. The exercise labels a two-premise biconditional rule LeftR but puts A-iff-B in the succedent; that formula's conclusion is incompatible with the rule label and with its premises. The weakening explanation calls Gamma entails Delta,A the end-formula of a proof although it is a sequent.
audited_source_corrections.chosen_treatment: Write A-and-B, Gamma in the contraction conclusion; write A-iff-B, Gamma entails Delta in the LeftR iff exercise; describe Gamma entails Delta,A as the end-sequent. Preserve both premises, the right iff exercise, all derivations, heights and other judgments.
audited_source_corrections.alternatives_considered: Keep the comma-free judgment; reinterpret the first iff rule as a right rule despite its label and counterexample; call a whole sequent a formula to avoid a token-key difference.
audited_source_corrections.rationale: The simulated G3c conjunction-left conclusion and both G1c intermediate contexts require a comma before Gamma. For left iff, if A and B have equal truth values, the two premises cover both-true and both-false cases; the corresponding conclusion has A iff B on the antecedent. The original right-side conclusion fails for A true and B false, when the second premise is true while the conclusion can be false. Gamma entails Delta,A is syntactically a sequent, not one formula.
audited_source_corrections.precise_review_question: Do the comma, left-iff conclusion and end-sequent wording repair only these three source slips while preserving the stated G1c/G3c admissibility and height arguments?
